hypothesis: A less regularized linear classifier or nonlinear RBF classifier may recover attribution information from frozen LUAR vectors. V5 weak transfer alone does not establish underfitting; training scores will be diagnostic only.
selection: Choose highest original-fold pooled balanced accuracy among exactly four recipes; ties follow declaration order. Check only that classifier and blend on robustness folds. No retuning.
pooling: Normalize logistic log probabilities or SVC OVR decision scores per row. Mix with separately renormalized completed v4 evidence using the declared weights. SVC is uncalibrated; no probability fitting.
diagnostics: Record per-fold training balanced accuracy, held-out balanced accuracy, iterations/support vectors and fitted SVC gamma. Diagnostics do not change candidate selection or thresholds.
limitations: Both validation partitions reuse labeled data and previously inspected splits; neither is an untouched holdout.
Selecting between four recipes introduces selection optimism; group-bootstrap intervals are descriptive only.
The cited paper does not establish transfer to this 18-class competition or guarantee any leaderboard gain.
No blind submission if the frozen gates fail. A later distinct experiment requires a separately recorded plan.
This follow-up was proposed after observing v5 failure and reuses its development labels; it adds further selection optimism.
